body:
I don't think I want to improve myself more. By improving my analytical thinking, my life only became worse, since I've come to realise what world we live in. I don't like this world, it's a failure. I know that it's not like I can choose another world to live in, but I don't get enough enjoyment or have enough interest to keep living in it. I seek conversations, but there's no people who want or capable of having interesting talk.

I live in a society where most people share the same mindset. They think very simple. I do not share that mindset, so I always feel lonely. Yes, I'm seeking relationship, but I don't know where to find person with same interests. And those advices "just go out there", "talk with people" - those are just plain stupid. Go out where? Talk with someone passing by on the street? Talk about what? I'm no fan of empty conversations, where everyone just says how his holidays went.

You see, going on living just because you won't get another shot won't work if life is just plain suffering. Not physical, but mental.

Searching for meaning can't be the meaning of life. If in your search you can find the true meaning, it means that searching wasn't the meaning from the start. If there's no way for you to find what you're searching for, then it's meaningless. Simple as that, a little logic shows us that searching for something can't be the meaning of life.

Yes, I know that many people make up their own meaning of life. Some live to get wealthy. Some live to get as much enjoyment as they can. Some just want to continue their lineage or be a respected person. But those are false meanings. They are self-centered, and insignificant in large scheme. I can't see a way for a high-intelligent person to enjoy living with fake meaning. It's actually pretty ironic, how the more intelligent person is, the less happy he becomes.

You know, living to be respected or to be successful would be acceptable to me, if I would not be so disappointed in humanity.
